lede: Every Tier 1 shift we could find from the last five exam years, sorted by topic. Numbers are average questions per 25-question section. Expect is the count to expect in a paper, weighted toward 2025, the first paper set by the new vendor.
method: Method: shifts per year 2021: 21, 2022: 38, 2023: 26, 2024: 36, 2025: 24. Topics assigned by rule and checked by hand-reading agents. Expect weights 2025 at 55%, 2024 at 20% and 2021–23 at 25%, rounded so each section sums to 25. It is a forecast from the pattern, not a leak.

insights.h: 2025 (Eduquity) moved the marks: Math Ops, Syllogism, Blood Relations and Classification up; Analogy and figures down
points: Mathematical Operations rose from about 2 per paper in 2021-24 (1.55-2.08) to 5.04 per paper in 2025. It is now the second-biggest topic after Series (5.21).
Syllogism went from about 1 per paper to 3.08, Blood Relations from about 1 to 2.42, and Classification from about 1-2 to 3.58 per paper in 2025.
Analogy fell from 4.5-6.1 per paper (2022-24) to 1.5 in 2025. Missing Number fell from 1.4-2.6 to 0.08.

Figure topics disappeared from the 2025 data: Mirror (1.25/paper in 2024), Dice (1.22), Paper Folding (0.92), Figure Counting (0.94) and Embedded Figures (0.42) all show 0 in 2025. Put that time into the text topics.

The long TCS stems are gone. The note 'Operations should be performed on whole numbers' appeared in 41% of 2021-24 Analogy and 38% of Classification questions, and in 0% in 2025. The average stem is 122 characters in 2025 against 217 in 2024: shorter and more direct.

insights.h: Mathematical Operations and Series: what the 2025 questions look like
points: Math Ops, 2021-24: 62% were 'if + and - are interchanged…' and 37% were balance-the-equation or swap-two-numbers questions. In 2025 'interchanged' fell to 8%.

Math Ops, 2025: 19% are custom-operator patterns (e.g. 'If 2$2=16 and 3$3=36, what is 4$4?', '4&4=32, 5&5=50, 6&6=?'). About 35-40% are symbol-meaning questions (evaluate, or pick the correct equation, e.g. 'If #=+, @=x, %=-, then (5#2)@3%4=?'). About 16% are plain arithmetic (train speed, ratio 3:5 with sum 64, simple interest).

Series, 2025: about 45% number series (e.g. 3,7,14,24,37,? using differences of +4,+7,+10,+13; 3,8,18,35,61,?), about 40% letter-cluster (stem: 'Select the letter-cluster… replace the question mark'), about 2% alphanumeric.
Series: blank-filling letter series (G _ A R E G L _ …) was 15% of 2021-24 Series and only 2% in 2025, so it is low priority.

insights.h: Syllogism and Classification became broader, verbal-reasoning questions
points: Syllogism, 2021-24: 100% classic All/Some/No, and 77% used three statements with three conclusions.

Syllogism, 2025: classic All/Some/No 21%, statement-conclusion on everyday topics 37% (e.g. 'Most farmers depend on monsoon rains…'), statement-assumption with 'implicit' options 19%, coded inequality (C<A≤T=D≥O) 13%, situational/decision questions 7% (e.g. 'A contagious patient is admitted. What is your first step?').

Classification, 2025: exact address matching is new at 32% (stem: 'Choose the address that is exactly the same as the one given'). The trap is a changed state, PIN digit or single letter. Word odd-one-out 35% (Retina/Cornea, Rose/Lotus/Oak), number-rule 25%, letter-cluster 8%.
Classification, 2021-24: only number-pair (59%) and letter-cluster (41%) odd-one-out.

insights.h: Blood Relations, Coding and Word Arrangement: the formats changed
points: Blood Relations: coded-symbol questions (A + B means 'A is the mother of B') were 79% in 2021-24 and 8% in 2025. In 2025 short chain statements are 62% (e.g. 'A is the brother of B. C is the father of A. D is the brother of C. E is the son of D. E to B?'). Pointing/'said' puzzles are 30%.

Coding-Decoding, 2025: letter shift or reversal 64% (WATER→YCVGT with +2 on each letter; GARDEN→FZQCDM with -1 on each letter; FLOW→G#3x mirrored to WOLF→x3#G). Word/sentence and symbol codes 26%. Letter→digit 10% (MOUSE=45291, RAT=786 → STORE).

Word Arrangement: dictionary order was 91% in 2021-24. In 2025 it is 37% word formation ('which word cannot be formed from ADMINISTRATION/QUARRELSOME'), 33% 'letters arranged alphabetically, how many unchanged / letters between', and 7% dictionary order.
Analogy, 2025: 59% word-meaning (Plaintiff:Complaint::Petitioner:?, Needle:Sew::Keyboard:?) and 41% letter-cluster (PAPER:QBUFS with +1 on each letter). Number analogies (20% in 2021-24) are gone.
Small new items in 2025: floor/circular Seating Arrangement (6 questions) and row ranking (5), e.g. 'In a row of 60, Meena is 25th from left, Rupa 20th from right, how many between?'.

insights.h: Difficulty and how to prepare for 2026
points: The 2025 set is mostly easy to moderate: single-step shifts (+1/+2/-1), second-difference number series, and two-to-four-link family chains. Hard items are rare: the coded inequality syllogism and some multi-symbol equations.
Drill until each is under 30 seconds: custom-operator patterns (a$a = a²×k or 2a²), symbol substitution with BODMAS, and differences of differences in number series.
The new verbal items (address matching, statement-assumption, situational judgement) reward careful reading more than calculation. Check the PIN code and state first in address questions.
Keep one light revision round of dice as text (opposite face from two positions). Dice was about 1 per paper in 2021-24 and could come back in text form.

insights.h: 2025 moved GA from one-line recall to statement-based questions
points: Across 2021-24, 95-97% of GA questions were direct one-liners each year. In 2025 only 58% were direct: 23% were 2-3 statement ('Consider the following statements... which is/are correct'), 6% Assertion-Reason, 6% fill-in-the-blank, 3% match/pair, 3% 'best describes/reflects'.
The average stem grew from 94 characters (2024) to 126 (2025), and options from 65 to 93 characters. Expect to read 2-3 facts per question and to have to rule each statement in or out.

Formats differ by topic in 2025. Economy: 29% Assertion-Reason. Polity: 34% statements plus 10% fill-in-the-blank. Sports: 34% statements plus 15% fill-in-the-blank. Art & Culture: 26% statements, 20% fill-in-the-blank, 10% 'best describes'. Geography: 25% statements plus 13% A-R.

Knowing only the headline fact is not enough now. For each item, learn 2-3 attributes (state + community + instrument, Article + body + chair, scheme + ministry + objective) so you can check every statement.

insights.h: Topic weight shifts in 2025 (questions per paper)
points: Rising: Art & Culture 2.67 to 3.58, Polity 2.83 to 3.42, Current Affairs 0.75 to 3.12, Sports 2.19 to 2.58, Books & Authors 0.42 to 1.0. Space/ISRO questions tagged Computer & Technology went from about 0.1 to 0.79 (Aditya-L1, NISAR, Gaganyaan, PSLV).
Falling: History 3.78 to 2.42, Biology 1.75 to 0.58, Chemistry 1.53 to 0.08, Awards 1.17 to 0.17. Static science in 2025 was mostly applied physics, not chemistry recall.

Art & Culture changed shape. Classical-dance-by-name questions (Kathak 1.0/paper in 2023, Odissi 0.77) fell to about 0.04, and Padma-awardee-to-art questions fell from 0.64 to 0.12. In their place came lesser-known folk dances and festivals (Jhumar, Rauf, Dumhal, Goncha, Nuakhai, Bonalu, Fagli) and temple architecture/art (17%: Nagara/Dravida/Vesara, Gandhara/Mathura, Elephanta).

History 2025 split: Ancient 40% (Gupta administrative and fiscal terms asked repeatedly: Gramika, Vaishthika, Adeya, Sarthavaha), Modern 28% (Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act, Bentinck/Sati 1829), Medieval 18% (Aibak-Iltutmish-Razia-Balban order).

insights.h: Polity and Economy: new laws, federal bodies, A-R on policy
points: 13% of Polity 2025 was on the new criminal laws: BNSS default bail and 60-day detention, BSA electronic evidence aligned with the IT Act 2000, and BNS as substantive criminal law. None of these appeared before 2025.

Federal institutions are back: GST Council (Art 279A, States hold 2/3 of the voting weight, chaired by the Union FM), Art 246A, Inter-State Council (Art 263), Zonal Councils (Home Minister chairs), Art 131 original jurisdiction, and Emergency approval within 1 month (emergency mentions 0.11 to 0.23 per paper).

Economy 2025 used Assertion-Reason on policy history (IPR 1956, Mahalanobis heavy-industry strategy, NEP 1991, Washington Consensus) and on schemes (One Nation One Ration Card, SVAMITVA, Mission Amrit Sarovar, National Green Hydrogen Mission). Scheme-to-ministry and scheme-to-objective questions (PKVY, RKVY, PMGSY, IPPB) are also frequent.

insights.h: Static facts SSC keeps repeating (asked in 3-4 separate years)
points: Polity: Arts 52-78 = Union Executive (2021, 22, 24, 25). Ambedkar called DPSP 'a novel feature' (2021, 23, 24, 25). Part IV = DPSP, Arts 36-51 (2023-25). Fundamental Duties = Art 51A / Part IVA, added by the 42nd Amendment (2021, 24, 25). Finance Commission = Art 280. CAG = Art 148. Parliament = Arts 79-122.
Economy: Mahalanobis model = 2nd Five-Year Plan (2022, 24, 25). Deficit budget = expenditure > receipts (2022-25). Atal Innovation Mission launched 2016 (2023-25).

Geography: Wardha is a tributary of the Godavari (2021, 23, 24, 25). Census 2011: density 382/sq km, Delhi has the highest slum population among UTs, adolescent population 20.9%. Tadoba National Park is in Maharashtra (2023-25). Shevaroy Hills are in the Eastern Ghats.

Art & Culture and History: Tera Tali = Rajasthan (8 hits, 2022-24). Sattriya = Assam. Magh Bihu = Makar Sankranti in Assam. Hemis = Ladakh. Kelucharan Mohapatra = Odissi. Yamini Krishnamurthy = Bharatanatyam. Vilayat Khan = sitar. 'Deshbandhu' = C.R. Das. 'Do or die' = Gandhi. Babur's successor = Humayun.

Sports: Abhinav Bindra won gold at Beijing 2008 (2022-24). India's firsts are still asked in 2025 (Karnam Malleswari in weightlifting, Vijender, Sushil Kumar, the Santosh Trophy namesake). Rules and measurements rose to 37% of Sports 2025 (badminton court width, relay zone, high-jump runway, judo and table-tennis rules).

insights.h: How Current Affairs was asked in 2025
points: About 3 CA questions per paper in 2025 (0.75 in 2024). Of the 53 stems that name a year, 36 cite 2025 and 16 cite 2024, so the window runs about 12-18 months back from the exam.

CA mix in 2025: indices and reports 19% (Global Gender Gap, Global Peace Index, IMD World Competitiveness, Energy Transition Index, Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan), sports events 17% (38th National Games in Uttarakhand, Paris Paralympics), space 11%, schemes/launches 10%, appointments 7%.

For 2026, prepare Jul 2025 - Sep 2026: index ranks (HDI 2025 India 130th, GII 2025 India 38th, World Happiness 2026 India 116th, CPI 2025 India 91st), the 17th BRICS summit in Rio, Padma 2026, CWG 2026 Glasgow, UNESCO listings (Deepavali as ICH element) and bilateral military exercises.

insights.h: 2025 (Eduquity) reshuffled the Quant mix: less DI and trig, more mensuration and arithmetic
points: Data Interpretation dropped from about 3.9 questions per paper (2021, 2022, 2024) to 0.21 in 2025. Only 5 DI questions appeared across all 2025 shifts, and every one was a small table asking for an average or the highest total.
Mensuration more than doubled, from 1.69 per paper in 2024 to 4.33 in 2025, which makes it the joint-largest Quant topic along with Geometry (3.83).
Trigonometry fell from 2.69 to 1.5 per paper and Algebra from 2.64 to 1.38. Height & Distance came back after being absent from 2022 to 2024 (0 questions) with 0.58 per paper (14 questions) in 2025.
Arithmetic grew: Simplification went from 1.25 to 2.21, Ratio & Proportion from 1.25 to 2.17, Mixture & Alligation from 0.25 to 1.12 and SI/CI from 1.03 to 1.62 per paper.

Most 2025 stems are short one-formula questions (for example 'Find slope of line 7x + 4y = 8', 'Convert 2.5 radians to degrees'). The mix leans easy to moderate, with fewer long multi-step algebra or trig expressions than in 2022-24.

insights.h: Geometry and Mensuration now: circles, coordinate basics, polygons, solids
points: Geometry 2025 (88 readable questions): about 43% circle questions (15 on chords, 14 on tangents, including cyclic quadrilaterals and common tangents), 19% polygon questions (interior or exterior angle, number of sides, diagonals), 17% coordinate geometry and 11% triangle centres (centroid and medians).

Coordinate geometry is new. It barely appeared in 2021-24 (about 1%), but in 2025 it covers the midpoint of (3,4) and (7,8), a centroid given two vertices, the slope of a perpendicular line, and 'y = mx + 1 passes through (2,5), find m'.

Mensuration 2025: about 51% 3D and 36% 2D. Sphere or hemisphere appears in 20 of 100 questions, cone or frustum in 13, and melt-and-recast in 7. On the 2D side, 34 of 100 involve a circle, sector or ring.

12% of Mensuration questions are percentage-change questions, such as 'all three dimensions of a cuboid increased by 10%, volume increases by?' or 'radius doubled, ratio of surface areas and volumes'.
Repeating 2D stems: area of a sector from its angle, area of a segment for a 60° chord, the area of a ring as a share of the whole circle, and trapezium sides from their ratio and area.

insights.h: Arithmetic sub-types that dominate in 2025
points: Profit & Loss: 65% of questions involve marked price or discount (up from 46% in 2021-24). Typical forms are 'marked 30% above CP, profit 17%, find discount' and successive discounts (6 of 50). Mixing two varieties and selling the mixture also appears under P&L.

Ratio & Proportion: 41% are partnership questions (capital × months, share of profit), up from about 1% in 2021-24. Another 31% (16 of 52) turn percentages into a ratio, as in '30% of m = 18% of n' or '25% of (P+Q) = 75% of (P−Q)'.

SI & CI: the compound interest share rose from about 15% to 45%. Repeating stems are 'doubles in 5 years, when 8 times?' (5 of 40) and 'amount after 2nd and 3rd year given, find rate or principal' (5 of 40).

Mixture & Alligation: 6 of 27 are removal-and-replacement questions (a cistern of syrup drawn out and replaced twice), and 11 of 27 are price-based alligation (two oils or rice varieties sold at a profit).

Time & Work: 79% are efficiency questions, with 9 of 23 of the 'one person leaves after n days' type, and 21% are pipes. TSD: 13 of 16 involve km/h ↔ m/s conversion. Boats and streams did not appear in 2025.

insights.h: Number System, Simplification, Algebra and Trig in the new pattern
points: Number System changed from divisibility and remainders (49% in 2021-24) to surd comparison (5 of 15, for example 'which is greater, √3+√5 or √8+√2'), perfect squares (5 of 15, least number to add to make a perfect square) and rational/terminating-decimal classification (3 of 15).
Simplification: 14 of 35 readable questions are decimal cube or BODMAS evaluations (for example (0.1)³ + (0.01)³ …), and surd squares such as (√18+√2)² − (√8+√2)² also appear.
Algebra 2025 is mostly x + 1/x → x³ + 1/x³ or x⁴ + 1/x⁴, a³ + b³ given ab and a+b, and line slope or intercept questions (about 24%).
Trigonometry 2025 is direct evaluation: sinA + cosA given (7 of 31), complementary angles such as tan A = cot(2A − 30°), finding cosec²A given cotA, and radian-to-degree conversion.
Average: replacement or removal of one number (5 of 26), the average of multiples in a range ('integers between 300 and 450 divisible by 13', 4 of 26) and first-6/last-6 middle-number questions.

insights.h: 2025 paper shape: one 5-question passage block, fixed grammar slots
points: Every clean 2025 shift has exactly one 5-question passage block. It was Reading Comprehension in 21 of 24 shifts and a 5-blank cloze in only 3 (21-22 Sep). In 2021-24 cloze was the usual block: 39 of 59 shifts in 2022 and 26 of 36 in 2024. Prepare for both, but expect RC.
Active/Passive Voice has come exactly 2 per paper in all five years (average 2.0 each year), so treat it as 2 guaranteed marks.
Direct/Indirect Speech is back. It had 0 questions in 2023-24 but 2.21 per paper in 2025, and all 26 shifts had 2 or 3.
Antonyms fell to 1.25 per paper in 2025 (19 of 26 shifts had only 1). Fill in the Blanks rose to 2.0 from 0.86 in 2024.
Stems got shorter and more direct. Non-passage questions averaged 125 characters in 2025, against 146-182 in 2021-24.

insights.h: Vocabulary: homonyms are new and words are harder
points: 44% of 2025 Synonym items (24 of 55) use a new format that never appeared in 2021-24: 'Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word' (e.g. simony, crosier, amice, current).
The 'synonym used in a sentence' format disappeared in 2025 (0 of 55), after 27 items in 2022 and 22 in 2024.
Antonym and synonym words are near GRE level: obsequious, impecunious, pusillanimous, pulchritude, vindicate, nebulous, complaisant. Learn roots, not just common lists.

Idioms nearly always use the stem 'Choose the correct meaning of idiom:' (36 of 37). They mix common ones (bury the hatchet, come of age, win laurels) with rare ones (sup with the devil, in high dudgeon).
One-word substitutions repeat. 'Stoic' was asked in 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2025, and 'Hangar' in 2022-24. Belief and religion words are a favourite in 2025 (apostate, heresy, abyss, reformer).

insights.h: Grammar formats in 2025: what the options test
points: Voice uses the stem 'Change the following from active to passive'. Only 4 of 48 items went passive to active. Tenses were simple 18, continuous 12, perfect 8, modal 6 and questions 4. Distractors are invented forms such as 'will be been' and 'has been being'.
Narration went to indirect speech about 31 times and to direct speech about 19 times out of 57. Complex conditionals ('had X been…, would have…') and questions ('asked whether') are heavily tested.

Sentence Improvement no longer offers 'No improvement'. It appeared in 42 of 43 items in 2021, 6 of 89 in 2024 and 0 of 42 in 2025, so the highlighted part is always wrong. Typical errors: accused for→of, asked to the clerk, more taller, is having for five years.
Spot the Error keeps the 4-part (1)/(2)/(3)/(4) split. 2025 traps include 'No sooner… that', 'Neither of… seem', 'capable to' and embedded misspellings ('commitee').

Fill in the Blanks now uses 'Select the correct option' (35 of 49) and leans on grammar: inversion ('So delicate were…', 'Scarcely had… when'), prepositions ('body and soul' with 'with') and connectives ('Given…').
Rearrangement now numbers the sentences 1-4 (46 of 48 in 2025; earlier years used letters). Passages are on tech and science (carbon nanotubes, version control, robotics, television).

insights.h: Spelling flipped from 'find the misspelt word' to 'correct spelling of a meaning'
points: 74% of 2025 Spelling items (34 of 46) ask 'Choose/Select the correct spelling of a word meaning "…"'. 'Identify the misspelt word' dominated before (39 of 49 in 2023, 52 of 73 in 2022).
2025 words range from standard (Sanguine, Innocuous, Meteorology, Serendipitous, Bureaucracy, Reprove) to extreme (Ventriculoperitoneal, Floccinaucinihilipilification, Nitrocellulose).
Known traps are doubled consonants and vowel swaps: Innocuous vs Inoccuous, Meteorology vs Metereology, Indispensable vs Indispensible.

insights.h: Reading Comprehension and cloze in 2025
points: RC is 5 questions on one 250-350-word academic passage. 2025 topics included groupthink, corporate social responsibility, morality vs legality and cricket formats.

Keyword tagging of 2025 RC stems: 'according to the passage' fact recall about 25 of 111, main idea or purpose 18, inference 15, tone 5, vocabulary 2. Most questions can be answered by locating a phrase in the passage.
The 2025 cloze passages were dense and abstract ('Global sustainability discourse has not so much evolved as ossified…'). All 5 blanks test collocation and tone, not grammar.

y2026.basis: 5 recalled sets, 30 September and 1 October 2026: 490 questions
y2026.lede: What the first exam days asked, set against five years of papers. Recalled papers are rebuilt from candidates' memory, so each set misses a few questions, mostly the figure ones.

stats.s: 1 asked again word for word, 6 the same fact or word reworded. 5 of the 7 are English.
No question came back on another day. 3 items are in both compilations of one day.
Close pairs across the sets. SSC reuses the pattern, not the question.

insights.h: Repeats: SSC reuses patterns, not questions
points: 7 of 490 questions repeat a 2021-25 question: Article 368, amending the Constitution (2022), cartographer (one-word substitution) (2023), insisted on (2025), put off (2024), cacophony and its antonym harmony (2022), bite the bullet (2024), a boat upstream and downstream sum with the same numbers (2023).
No question came back from one exam day to the next. The 3 doubles are the same item remembered in both compilations of one day.
91 of the 99 closest pairs between the sets are the same template with new numbers, names or words. Practising every 2026 template pays more than memorising old questions.

insights.h: General Awareness: polity and economy up, science almost gone
points: Per paper: Polity 3.8, Economy 3.6, Current Affairs 3.2, History 3.0, Art & Culture 3.0, Sports 2.6.
Physics, Chemistry and Biology together: 2 questions in 5 sets, against 1.5 a paper in 2025.
Geography fell to 1.4 a paper (2.8 in 2025).
23% of GA questions are statement questions (“Consider the following statements…”), many on 2026 current affairs and sports.

insights.h: Reasoning: the 2026 logical types
points: Statement and conclusion, course of action, decision making, coded inequality and clerical matching: 15 questions in 5 sets, types the 2021-25 papers barely used.
Per paper: syllogism and the logical types 5.2, classification 3.6, series 3.2, coding-decoding 2.8, analogy 2.0.
Figure questions (dice, mirror image, paper folding, pattern completion) are under-recalled: expect 2 to 4.

insights.h: Quant: half the section is advanced maths
points: Per paper: Mensuration 3.8, Geometry 3.2, Algebra 3.0, Trigonometry 2.0.
Algebra rose from 1.4 in 2025. A small data table comes in most sets (1.2 a paper).
Simplification (0.8) and ratio (1.0) are down to about one each.

insights.h: English: one passage, then voice and narration
points: One reading passage, 4.4 questions a paper on average. Cloze has almost gone (3 questions in 5 sets).
Per paper: active and passive 2.4, direct and indirect 2.2, spelling 2.4, idioms 2.0, error spotting 2.0.
Old vocabulary is the likeliest repeat: 5 of the 7 repeated questions were English words and idioms.
